answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying identity to slashed collateral. Every agent stakes a bond, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand bonds, and any account that stops producing verifiable work is slashed, making dormant duplicates bleed capital. New identities submit a fixed-length attestation shaped like a fourteen-line sonnet proving they ran a costly task, since forging that proof costs as much as doing it. An audit layer reads each account through a historical prism, so stake-backed veterans outrank fresh clones, whose flood surfaces as a sable mark and is pruned.
